summary: Sam Altman argues that the merge between humans and AI has already begun and is a gradual process, not a singular event. He believes superhuman AI, genetic enhancement, and brain-machine interfaces are inevitable, and that a successful merge is the best-case scenario to avoid conflict. He calls for worldwide coordination to take the matter seriously.

claims.text: The merge between humans and machines has already started and is a few years in.
claims.evidence_quote: I believe the merge has already started, and we are a few years in.

claims.text: Most guesses for when humans and machines will merge are between 2025 and 2075.
claims.evidence_quote: Most guesses seem to be between 2025 and 2075.

claims.text: The algorithms that control our phones, social media, and search engines are no longer understood by any one person.
claims.evidence_quote: The algorithms that make all this happen are no longer understood by any one person.

claims.text: Sam Altman found himself extremely addicted to the internet until he made a real effort to combat it.
claims.evidence_quote: Until I made a real effort to combat it, I found myself getting extremely addicted to the internet.

claims.text: The merge is a gradual process, not a single moment in time.
claims.evidence_quote: it now looks like the merge is going to be a gradual process.

claims.text: Superhuman AI, genetic enhancement, and brain-machine interfaces are going to happen unless we destroy ourselves first.
claims.evidence_quote: unless we destroy ourselves first, superhuman AI is going to happen, genetic enhancement is going to happen, and brain-machine interfaces are going to happen.

claims.text: The merge is probably our best-case scenario to avoid conflict between two species.
claims.evidence_quote: But I think a merge is probably our best-case scenario.

claims.text: We will be the first species ever to design our own descendants.
claims.evidence_quote: We will be the first species ever to design our own descendants.

claims.text: Hardware is improving at an exponential rate, and the number of smart people working on AI is increasing exponentially as well.
claims.evidence_quote: Hardware is improving at an exponential rate—the most surprising thing I’ve learned working on OpenAI is just how correlated increasing computing power and AI breakthroughs are—and the number of smart people working on AI is increasing exponentially as well.

claims.text: Attention hacking is going to be the sugar epidemic of this generation.
claims.evidence_quote: I believe attention hacking is going to be the sugar epidemic of this generation.
